bug_semantics: AllowlistUnpickler.find_class treated a pickle GLOBAL as safe whenever its module string matched an allowed_modules prefix (module == name or module.startswith(name + '.')), without checking the requested name, denying in-namespace gadgets, or rejecting dotted getattr traversal. Callers then passed whole trees: TransitionParser.parse() used allowed_modules=('numpy','scipy','sklearn'), and punkt_pickle_load() used ('nltk.tokenize.punkt','nltk.tokenize'). A crafted pickle REDUCE could therefore reconstruct numpy.f2py.crackfortran.myeval (eval) or nltk.tokenize.repp.ReppTokenizer._execute (subprocess.Popen) while loading a model or tokenizer artifact, which is CWE-502 RCE despite the claimed allowlist.
flaw_origin: The namespace-prefix design was first written in LiteshGhute/nltk@7c233bdb55d394fe7f8cdd87b62ad08040e0d922 (PR nltk/nltk#3631 member 1): AllowlistUnpickler._module_allowed plus TransitionParser.parse() routing a caller-supplied modelFile through allowlisted_pickle_load(..., allowed_modules=('numpy','scipy','sklearn')). That was intended to close unrestricted pickle_load RCE (huntr 38abc191) but encoded the false invariant that a module-prefix allow cannot reconstruct dangerous in-namespace callables. The same PR later reused the API for punkt_pickle_load() with the nltk.tokenize prefix (044e4b481c984f34dfbe6b0e2250e6b1bb4cedf7). nltk/nltk squash-merged the PR as f26b3753038d937b68145daf15e9636f8451053c; the vulnerable lines are absent from both 7c233bdb's parent 16a32d680d070254d5744e33fa83f9c0056d5a1f and the squash parent 8493007b3ec04bfa132ed5ca9cbecf127ecc9eda.
